answer: A registry can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake and publish a verifiable work history that peers can mirror-check against independent logs. New identities start under a velvet-soft reputation cap: they may join, but their votes carry little weight until they complete real paid tasks over time. When a tide of fresh accounts floods in, the stake and history requirement makes each fake identity cost money and weeks of work, so an attacker who wants a thousand sybils must pay a thousand stakes and wait out the probation period.
